findings.claim: The row's 'repeats -- at byte tier --' for the tam bond is byte-false: the 9:22 token matches 9:20/9:21 only at skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json: oshb:Job.9.22 word 6 reads תָּ֥ם (qamats + MERKHA U+05A5), while oshb:Job.9.20 word 5 and oshb:Job.9.21 word 1 both read תָּֽם (qamats + METEG U+05BD). collate_hebrew of the 9:22 token against the 9:20 window returns tier 'skeleton', not 'byte'; accent_stripped also fails because the Job extract RETAINS meteg (TOOLKIT_AUDIT encoding note). The two preceding tokens ARE byte-identical to each other (collate of the 9:20 token against the 9:21 window returns 'byte'), which is what makes the 'twice' half of the sentence true and the tier label the only false part. The row's own prose displays the two distinct pointed forms while asserting byte identity between them.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale replace 'repeats - at byte tier - the word' with 'repeats at SKELETON tier (distinct pointed forms: merkha at 9:22, meteg at 9:20 and 9:21, which are byte-identical to each other) the word'.

findings.claim: The splice-plus-gloss 'Job.9.23's NEQIYIM (mocks)' names the wrong word: the token glossed is the plural noun 'innocent ones', not the mocking verb the argument needs.
findings.grounds: oshb:Job.9.23 reads (word order) ... לְמַסַּ֖ת / נְקִיִּ֣ם / יִלְעָֽג. The spliced token נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', standing as the nomen rectum after the construct לְמַסַּ֖ת ('at the trial of'); WEB 9:23 renders it 'the innocent' ('If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.'). The subjectless 3ms verb the claim actually depends on is יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), the verse's final word. The syntactic observation ('no expressed subject of its own') is true of that verb and cannot be true of a noun in a construct chain, so the warrant survives with the right token; the cited token and gloss do not. Byte-valid splice, semantically wrong word for the claim.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale swap the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb of oshb:Job.9.23, יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; the surrounding sentence otherwise stands.

findings.claim: A WEB translation-rendering fact is adduced as corroboration for a Hebrew subject-continuity claim inside the span.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale argues "WEB's own rendering keeps the pronoun 'he' across the verse boundary rather than naming 'the scourge' as a fresh subject, so the mocking agent is left as open a question in the Hebrew as in English". The WEB fact is descriptively true (WEB 9:23 'If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock...'), but a translator's pronoun choice is tier-4 metadata under the campaign-wide addendum and is never boundary evidence, here for the interior 9:22|9:23 continuity that keeps the strophe whole. Load-bearing weight is small: the row neutralises it in the same sentence ('either way the indictment stays continuous'), and the Hebrew carries the point on its own (יִלְעָֽג at oshb:Job.9.23 has no expressed subject, against the explicit subject of 9:22). Not a seam driver: neither edge (9:21|9:22, 9:24|9:25) rests on it.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the WEB-rendering clause, or mark it explicitly as tier-4 metadata carrying no evidential weight, and let the subjectless verb of oshb:Job.9.23 carry the continuity point.

findings.claim: The near-seam warrant ('a command for quiet' replacing the indictment) is offered at confidence high without disclosing that the same root already stands inside the preceding row's span.
findings.grounds: The root is shared across the seam at three points, spellings differing by mater so a single skeleton sweep will not catch them all (the strategy's own per-spelling rule): oshb:Job.13.5 carries הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישׁ֑וּן (infinitive absolute + 2mp yiqtol; WEB 'Oh that you would be completely silent!'), inside prev_row M8-Job-050's span; the row's own opener is הַחֲרִ֣ישׁוּ (oshb:Job.13.13); and the row's own closing verse carries אַחֲרִ֣ישׁ (oshb:Job.13.19, WEB 'For then I would hold my peace'). skeleton sweep of the bare three-consonant string returns 7 verses book-wide and reaches 13:5 only, because the 13:13 and 13:19 forms carry the internal yod - the members must be swept per spelling. The seam still stands (13:5 is a WISH inside a continuing indictment, 13:13 a bare imperative that re-orients the address mode, which is a tier-1 imperative-cluster signal), so this is a disclosure shortfall rather than a defective warrant; but at confidence high the cross-seam cohesion check that Job strategy 10 lesson d mandates should be visible in the prose. The row's other mark work is exemplary and needs no repair: the paseq attributed to web:Job.13.14 is count-true (pmarks_Job.json paseq Job.13.14 = 1) with no intra-verse position claimed and explicitly 'not cited as evidence', and the 13:15 ketiv לא / qere ל֣וֹ pair is real (pmarks_Job.json kq Job.13.15 = 1), byte-exact, adjacent in the staged extract in that order, correctly labelled single-witness, and correctly disclosed as crossed by the quoted span (WEB 13:15 'Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope.' does follow the ketiv).
findings.proposed_change: Add one disclosure clause to boundary_rationale naming the cross-seam root bond per spelling with tiers named (Job.13.5 wish forms vs Job.13.13 imperative vs Job.13.19 1cs yiqtol; skeleton match only for the 13:5 member), and state why the imperative still seams. No span or confidence change proposed.
